findings.issue: The app ships with no tests, no test script and no test runner; all filtering, pagination, sorting, URL-state and error logic is guarded only by the external acceptance suite.
findings.suggestion: Add Vitest (TanStack's own setup-testing guide recommends vitest + @testing-library/react) and start with unit tests for the pure layer: format.ts and the getHomeData/getPokemonPageData data builders against a mocked fetch.

findings.issue: Server-function validators are type-only passthroughs ((data) => data), so unvalidated client input reaches the pagination math directly.
findings.suggestion: Either add real runtime validation (page is a finite integer, type/generation are strings) or unit-test getHomeData with hostile inputs; today a non-numeric page from a direct serverFn call yields Math.min(NaN, totalPages) = NaN and an empty item list.

findings.issue: isNotFound only maps status 404 to a Not-found page; any other API failure (500, network error) is rethrown and surfaces as an unhandled server error with no error boundary or tested fallback.
findings.suggestion: Add an error-path test (or at least a NotComponent/defaultErrorComponent in the router) and decide what a non-404 failure renders.

findings.issue: The alternate-form exclusion (id > 10000) is duplicated by hand at four call sites (getHomeData type filter, getMovePageData, getAbilityPageData, getTypePageData) with no shared predicate or test.
findings.suggestion: Extract a single isDefaultForm(id) helper and cover it with tests including boundary ids 10000 and 10001; a refactor that changes one site but not the others would silently leak Megas into lists.

findings.issue: The in-memory promise cache (eviction on failure via promise.catch(() => cache.delete(url))) has no tests: nothing pins that a rejected fetch is evicted and retried, or that concurrent calls share one request.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test apiGet with a stubbed fetch: assert single flight for parallel calls and that a 500 does not poison the cache for subsequent requests.

findings.issue: Null-handling exists in two places (compareValues and again in the useMemo comparator), so the compareValues branch is partially dead; a refactor to one of them can break 'missing values sort last when descending' undetected.
findings.suggestion: Hoist the null-last rule into one comparator and unit-test it for both directions, including all-null pairs.

findings.issue: trackable, formatHeight, formatWeight and compareText are dead exports — the same formatting is re-implemented inline at app/src/lib/data.server.ts:576-577 and 640-642, so the two copies can drift.
findings.suggestion: Use the helpers (or delete them) and unit-test the single source of truth for the '0.4 m' / '6.0 kg' / em-dash formats.

findings.issue: The debounce effect disables react-hooks/exhaustive-deps and depends on search.type/search.generation to re-arm; the guard (query !== search.q) is the only thing preventing a redundant navigation on filter changes.
findings.suggestion: Cover this with a component test that types a query, changes the type filter, and asserts exactly one URL transition and that page resets to 1.

summary: The app contains no tests of its own: no runner, no script, no spec files, so nothing the team owns will fail when the data layer is refactored. The riskiest logic — home filtering and pagination math, move-table sorting, learn-method ordering, alternate-form exclusion, URL-state handling and the promise cache — is entirely unguarded, and some of it (passthrough serverFn validators, 404-only error mapping) has real edge-case bugs waiting. Adding Vitest unit coverage of format.ts and the data.server.ts builders against a mocked fetch would be the highest-value first step.
